symptoms: Backend-only releases could wait for an irrelevant website deployment SHA.
The public connector readiness endpoint returned HTTP 503 during production release readback.
A stale production deploy could be mistaken for a successful release when deployment state was not tied back to the exact release SHA.

root_causes.cause: Production readback originally coupled all releases to website deployment state instead of the canonical affected delivery lanes.
The authenticated /api/connectors/* wildcard could overlap the public /api/connectors/readiness route until readiness was explicitly excluded.
A single transient 5xx response could create a false-red production release signal.
Repository tests and Brain scripts referenced a canonical migration path that was absent from git even though a corresponding migration existed remotely.

invariants: Backend-only releases MUST NOT wait for an unrelated website SHA.
Any Netlify-hosted runtime change MUST require an exact production deployment proof.
/api/connectors/readiness MUST remain public and MUST be excluded from /api/connectors/*.
Readiness retries MUST be bounded and MUST still fail closed after the retry budget or on an invalid contract.
A release MUST NOT be called live from merge or deploy state alone; exact-SHA production readback is authoritative.
Any canonical migration referenced by tests or Brain scripts MUST exist in the repository.
incidents.learning_rule: Every production failure must end in a machine-enforced invariant and regression test; narrative documentation alone is insufficient.
